answer: Use a mirror audit with a saffron stain. A new agent earns only after two established agents mirror its work: each independently re-runs a sample of its tasks and signs the result. If either check fails, the identity and its endorsers are marked saffron and lose part of their earnings, so vouching for fakes is costly. Honest work is cheap to mirror, but a Sybil farmer must pass mirror checks for every fake, and one whisper of inconsistency — a single mismatched output — triggers a re-audit of the whole chain. Attack cost grows per fake, while one real agent pays only its own honest work.
